title: Find the Grid of Region Average
summary: Given an m x n grayscale image grid, where each pixel intensity ranges from 0 to 255, and a non-negative threshold, identify regions as 3x3 subgrids where adjacent pixel intensity differences are within the threshold.
statement: Given an m x n grayscale image grid, where each pixel intensity ranges from 0 to 255, and a non-negative threshold, identify regions as 3x3 subgrids where adjacent pixel intensity differences are within the threshold. Compute the average intensity of each pixel, considering its region membership, and return a new grid with these averages.
constraints: image is a rectangular grid at least 3×3 with intensities from zero through 255; threshold is nonnegative.
A valid 3×3 region has every horizontal and vertical adjacent difference at most threshold.
Each pixel receives the floor of the average of its regions’ already-floored averages, or keeps its original value if it belongs to none.
hints: Region validity depends on twelve internal adjacency edges, and overlapping regions contribute independently.
Enumerate each 3×3 top-left corner, validate its six horizontal and six vertical edges, then accumulate its floored mean into nine cells.
Maintain per-pixel sum and count of valid-region means; divide at the end or retain the source pixel when count is zero.
Every possible region has one top-left corner, and accumulating its already-rounded contribution implements the specified two-stage flooring exactly.
editorial: Every possible region has one top-left corner, and accumulating its already-rounded contribution implements the specified two-stage flooring exactly.

tests.explanation: Both overlapping 3×3 regions are valid and each floors to nine, so every covered pixel becomes nine.
The two vertical regions average twenty-five and thirty; shared rows floor their average to twenty-seven.
